title: Orient Bell Ltd-$ - 530365 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Orient Bell Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 66% YoY to INR16.4 crores, with margin up 270 bps, after ~20% cumulative price hikes in March-April.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes grew 7% and revenue rose 7.5% YoY, with FY26 volumes up 4.4% and revenue up 3.1%. Consolidated EBITDA for Q4 was INR16.4 crores (up 66% YoY, margin up 270 bps) and PBT was INR8.4 crores versus INR3.6 crores a year earlier. Management took roughly 20% cumulative price increases in March and April to offset a roughly 30% rise in gas prices, and said the company is debt free with surplus cash. Management declined to give forward guidance on volumes, margins or capacity utilisation, citing gas-supply uncertainty in Morbi.

vs INR3.8 crores in FY25; after INR1.3 crores one-time labour code cost

financial_highlights.metric: Incremental revenue flow-through to bottom line

financial_highlights.value: Debt free; negative debt of INR29 crores on books

segments.name: Retail vs institutional
segments.commentary: Retail was about 78% of FY26 revenue, with institutional the balance. Management said retail grew faster while the enterprise business did not do well in FY26.

segments.name: Vitrified vs non-vitrified
segments.commentary: Vitrified utilisation was about 80% per management's estimate; non-vitrified was not quantified but was described as higher, possibly around 90% in Q4.

segments.name: Adhesives
segments.commentary: Still in pilot-stage expansion in select North and East India geographies; epoxy, grout and spatula added in the last 2-3 months. Management expects decent volumes in FY27 but gave no figures.

segments.name: Anti-static and antimicrobial tiles
segments.commentary: Some orders received, but management said contribution remains very small and not enough to move the top line.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance on sales growth, volumes or capacity utilisation for FY27; management said it does not give forward guidance.
Management expects Q1 FY27 to see the remaining part of the gas/energy cost increase, since cost increases began around 9-10 March and part was covered in Q3 and Q4.
Management said there is no downward price movement likely in the next few months, and definitely not in Q1, as Gujarat gas June pricing is expected to rise about INR5 per cubic metre.
Management expects FY26 margins to be better than FY25, and said margins have improved year-on-year for the last three quarters.
Capex: no major capacity capex needed in FY27; maintenance capex is about INR10 crores plus or minus INR4-5 crores versus about INR6-7 crores in FY26.
Marketing spend is expected to rise from 3.6% of revenue toward about 4% in FY27, though this is not yet decided.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation was about 60-65% in Q4 FY26, and management said it is better than in Q3 and April-May is better than Q4.
No major capacity capex needed; capex limited to maintenance, about INR6-7 crores in FY26 and about INR10 crores plus or minus INR4-5 crores in FY27.
Company has three factories outside the Morbi cluster, which supply the bulk of sales and helped stock availability.

Gas allocation was cut to about 50% at one point roughly 10 weeks before the call, leading management to consider shutting some lines; the company uses biofuels in spray dryers at Sikandrabad for 7-8 years.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price increase of about 20% in March and April 2026 (about 15-16% in March, 5-6% in April); the company said it was among the first to raise prices around 10 March.
Management said all cost increases have been passed on to consumers so far, and further increases depend on gas prices.
Dealers are cautious and reducing stock to avoid high-priced inventory; a dealer working-capital squeeze and wait-and-watch behaviour in large projects were cited.

Morbi: over 500 units reopened from 1 May, mostly GVT; ceramic output is lower, with labour shortages constraining polishing and packing. Management said Morbi design-level stocks have run down after no production in late March and April.
Management said Morbi oversupply has been cut by the crisis; exports were flat in FY26 and the unorganised sector did poorly.
Digital initiatives: 50,000 new designs added monthly by dealers via AI room visualisation; online lead generation contributing sales for 350-plus dealers monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins sustain around Q4 levels given gas price pressure, and have price hikes been taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the margin trajectory to continue; Q4 margin was 7.7% versus about 6% in Q3 (per management's description). Price hikes of about 20% were taken in March-April and further gradual increases are expected depending on gas and diesel prices.

qa_highlights.question: What are gas prices and the Q4 blended INR per SCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas pricing is formula-linked and changes every few days, with the mix moving from 80% formula to 55% normal and 45% spot. Overall gas prices are up about 30%, and Q4 blended cost averaged about INR45 per SCM.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company undertake capex now that debt is repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: No capacity capex is needed in FY27 given existing capacity; capex will be for maintenance, around INR10 crores plus or minus INR4-5 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue goes to marketing?
qa_highlights.answer: Marketing was 3.6% of revenue in FY26 and is expected to creep up toward about 4%, with no final decision taken.

qa_highlights.question: Will capacity utilisation rise above 80% and will the company gain share from unorganised players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide on FY27 utilisation, citing gas uncertainty. It said it is better placed to gain share from Morbi disruption due to its balance sheet and sell-out model, and that OBTX share could rise, though it has not quantified the split.

qa_highlights.question: How are price hikes expected to play out, and is there demand slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects realisations to readjust over about 3-4 months as gas costs normalise; tile is 1-2% of project cost, so customers are not expected to defer purchases. Management said it has seen no demand slowdown, with the Q4 volume growth figure cited.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR1.28 crore exceptional item and the fall in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: The exceptional item is the one-time labour code provision for retirement benefits at 50% of salary. Other expenses fell to INR31.8 crores from INR33.6 crores in Q4, mainly from lower travel and design costs; FY26 other expenses were at a similar level to FY25.

risks_watch: Gas price volatility and allocation cuts; formula-linked pricing changes every few days, and June Gujarat gas pricing is expected to rise about INR5 per cubic metre.
Demand after price hikes of about 20%: dealer destocking, working-capital squeeze and project wait-and-watch behaviour.
Q1 FY27 margin impact from the remaining energy cost increase, as cost increases began 9-10 March.
Morbi reopening pace and labour constraints, which could change competitive pricing; some pricing may reverse as gas costs ease within about 3-4 months.
Adhesives and anti-static product contribution remains small; the adhesive business is still at pilot stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, the balance sheet and market share opportunity, but cautious and evasive on forward guidance, citing gas-supply uncertainty; management repeatedly declined to give FY27 volume, margin or utilisation numbers.
key_quotes: Our strong balance sheet and success in cost management enables us to manage any volatility which might be seen in the short-term.
As utilization levels continue to improve, the benefit of operating leverages are becoming increasingly visible in the business.
So as of now, we have passed on all the cost increase to the consumer.

growth.why: Management gave no numerical FY27 guidance on sales, volumes or utilisation, and no major capacity additions are planned (no major capacity capex needed in FY27, maintenance capex only ~INR10 crore); Q4 utilisation ~60-65% leaves ample spare capacity, while Q4 revenue grew 7.5% YoY and EBITDA 66% on ~20% price hikes.
